name: Kozel (Russian Goat)
description: Kozel (Russian for 'Goat') is a highly aggressive Russian trick-taking game played with 36 cards. It is a descendant of the German game 'Bura' and is distinguished by its unique rule allowing players to lead multiple cards of the same suit simultaneously. It is an 'Ace-Ten' game where the objective is to capture point cards, and the loser is mocked as the 'Goat'.

content.text: Kozel (Russian for 'Goat') is a highly aggressive Russian trick-taking game played with 36 cards. It is a descendant of the German game 'Bura' and is distinguished by its unique rule allowing players to lead multiple cards of the same suit simultaneously. It is an 'Ace-Ten' game where the objective is to capture point cards, and the loser is mocked as the 'Goat'.
Dates to the early 20th century in Russia. It shares DNA with Bura and common Russian gambling games developed in naval and prison environments.
36 cards. Rank: Ace (11), Ten (10), King (4), Queen (3), Jack (2). 9s, 8s, 7s, 6s = 0 points.
